history: Discovered in 2489 by a survey drone that nearly missed the dim brown dwarf entirely, the system was initially catalogued as worthless.
Smugglers discovered the natural EM dampening field in 2567 and established Haven as a meeting point beyond faction jurisdiction.
The colony on Hollow was founded by refugees from the Corporate Wars who wanted to disappear; their descendants maintain the tradition of anonymity.
description: Whisperwind Hollow barely qualifies as a star system—its brown dwarf primary emits so little light that the system exists in perpetual twilight, visible only in infrared to unaugmented eyes. The Whisper hangs in the void like a cooling ember, deep magenta and slowly fading, providing just enough warmth through tidal heating to keep Hollow's subsurface ocean liquid. Two ice worlds orbit this failed star, one harboring a hidden colony, the other a captured wanderer on a centuries-long elliptical path. The system's natural EM dampening field—The Silence—makes it nearly invisible to long-range sensors.

This obscurity is the system's primary value. Haven station serves those who need to conduct business away from prying eyes: smugglers, information brokers, fugitives, and the occasional legitimate merchant seeking tax-free transactions. The colony on Hollow asks no questions about residents' pasts; citizenship is available to anyone who contributes, and records are kept on paper that burns. The 23,000 inhabitants live in domed cities beneath the ice, sustained by geothermal energy and hydroponic farms, connected to the wider galaxy only when they choose to be.

No faction claims Whisperwind Hollow because no faction knows precisely where it is—the EM dampening field affects outgoing signals as well as incoming, making navigation data intentionally imprecise. Visitors must know someone who knows the way. This isolation provides security but also vulnerability; if trouble finds Whisperwind Hollow, no help will come. The colonists maintain defensive systems and emergency evacuation protocols, but their true protection is obscurity. In a galaxy of brilliant stars and bustling systems, sometimes the safest place is a hollow whisper in the dark.
